blocks.text: Leaving an infected tooth untreated means you’re facing even bigger risks, like a widespread infection or tooth loss. If that infection involves your tooth root, our dentist in Wyoming, OH, at Wyoming Family Dentistry can provide root canal therapy to treat this condition. It’s a common — and highly successful — procedure that helps prevent the need for tooth removal.
This procedure involves removing infected/decayed material from inside your tooth to address infections. During this process, we clear out and clean the canals in the pulp of your tooth.
When Might You Need Root Canal Therapy?
Do you have a severe cavity or cracked tooth? If decay or damage affects the root of your tooth, we may recommend this treatment. Some signs that you might need it include:

items: Tooth pain, especially when you bite down or chew
Facial or jaw pain on the affected side
A bump or pimple on your gums near the affected tooth

blocks.text: What Happens During a Root Canal?

Getting root canal therapy in Wyoming, OH, begins with making a small hole in the tooth so we can access the inner part. Once we’re inside, we eliminate the infection from the pulp and completely disinfect the area.
When everything’s cleared out and cleaned, we fill the spaces with dental material and close up the tooth, placing a crown on it for protection.

They do have a reputation for this. But root canals have come a long way, providing a treatment approach that’s no more uncomfortable than getting a filling. We numb the area so you won’t feel anything, though you might have mild soreness afterward.
What Are the Benefits of Getting a Root Canal?

Treating infections before they get worse is always the best solution. Root canals do this when infections reach deep inside your tooth, preventing more severe complications and allowing you to keep your natural tooth.
Visit Our Dentist for Root Canal Therapy

Do you have a painful or infected tooth that’s not improving? At Wyoming Family Dentistry, our dental team offers root canal therapy in Wyoming, OH, as a way to eliminate tooth infections near the root and save your natural teeth!
